series_manifest.label: Import Price Index (Price of Goods Brought into US)

events.label: Global trade collapse: import prices fall 23%
COVID shutdowns: imports drop to $169 billion
Imports and import prices near pandemic-era highs
Record $342 billion of imports ahead of tariffs

explanation.summary: How much the US spends on goods from abroad each month, and how the prices of those goods change. The stripes below show every month since 2006: red means higher than a year before, blue means lower. The two rise and fall together in the same month. Part of this is built in: when import prices go up, the same goods cost more dollars.
explanation.methodology: Monthly value of goods imports (balance of payments basis) from the Census Bureau and BEA via FRED (BOPGIMP). Import price index for all imports from BLS (EIUIR). Port wait-time data is not published through any public federal API, so it is not shown.

key_findings.title: 2009: Trade Collapses
key_findings.description: Monthly imports fell from $198 billion (July 2008) to $124 billion (June 2009). Import prices dropped 23% in just five months, from 148 to 114.
key_findings.significance: In a deep recession, both the amount and the price of imports fall together.

key_findings.title: 2022: Pandemic Buying Boom
key_findings.description: Americans bought goods instead of services. Imports reached $282 billion a month, and import prices rose 25% from their April 2020 low, to 148.
key_findings.significance: Strong demand plus clogged supply chains pushed up prices of goods from abroad.

key_findings.title: March 2025: Record Imports
key_findings.description: Imports hit a record $342 billion in one month as companies rushed to bring in goods before new tariffs took effect.
key_findings.significance: Policy announcements can pull purchases forward and create sudden spikes.
